questions.question: With semi-synchronous replication (default AFTER_SYNC wait point), what must happen before the source returns COMMIT to the client?
options: Every replica must apply the transaction
At least one replica must acknowledge it received and wrote the transaction to its relay log
The transaction must be written to a physical backup
questions.explanation: Semi-sync waits for at least one replica to receive and persist the events in its relay log, not to apply them.

questions.question: Why is ROW the recommended binlog format?
options: It always produces the smallest binlog
It stores the SQL text so replicas can re-optimise queries
It records actual row changes, so nondeterministic statements replicate safely
It disables the need for primary keys
questions.explanation: ROW logs before/after row images, so functions like UUID() or LIMIT without ORDER BY cannot produce different results on replicas. It can be larger than STATEMENT for bulk updates.

questions.question: What does `mysqldump --single-transaction` rely on to produce a consistent InnoDB backup without locking tables?
options: FLUSH TABLES WITH READ LOCK held for the whole dump
questions.explanation: It starts a consistent snapshot transaction under REPEATABLE READ, so all tables are read as of one point in time while writes continue.

questions.question: Which of these can NOT be supplied as a `?` placeholder in a prepared statement?
options: A customer email in a WHERE clause
questions.explanation: Placeholders bind values only. Identifiers and keywords such as ORDER BY directions must be validated against an allow-list.
